clue.text: End the fighting

definitions.meaning: to end a plan or project is to abandon or discard it
a fight or brawl, informally a scuffle

explanation.surface: A call to stop the fighting and make peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap something is to drop it altogether, and a scrap is a brief scuffle.

clue.text: Discerning something Forsytish at the start

definitions.text: Discerning something Forsytish at the start

parts.words: Discerning something Forsytish at the start
parts.note: Galsworthy's Forsytes appear in a long family chronicle, and that word for a chronicle opens a word for discerning

explanation.surface: A shrewd reader spots echoes of the Forsyte novels early on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forsyte Saga is Galsworthy's novel sequence; SAGA begins the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacious means wise and shrewd in judgement.

clue.text: Whence Blake plucked his rural pen

definitions.text: Whence Blake plucked his rural pen

parts.words: Whence Blake plucked his rural pen
parts.note: in Blake's introduction to Songs of Innocence, 'I plucked a hollow reed, And I made a rural pen'

explanation.surface: Where William Blake found his country writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall grasses of marsh and riverbank, from whose hollow stems Blake made a pen.

clue.text: Baggy panto character

parts.note: the foolish old man of the harlequinade, whose name gave us the word for baggy trousers

explanation.surface: A loose-costumed figure in a Christmas pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British Christmas stage show; Pantaloon, the old dotard of the harlequinade, gave his name to loose trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: The doddering old man of Italian comedy and the harlequinade, worn in loose breeches.

clue.text: The beggar's so submissive !

parts.note: a beggar humbly holds out headgear for coins, and the phrase for that pose also means meekly deferential

explanation.surface: A remark on how meek a beggar looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes approaching someone humbly to ask a favour, as a beggar holds out a hat.

clue.text: Right among the old hens' note, there's a sharp report

indicators.note: among means placed within, so one letter goes inside the hens' sound

parts.note: a cackle is the noise hens make

explanation.surface: Amid clucking hens a gunshot rings out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a bang, not an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackle is a series of sharp snapping sounds, like gunfire or burning twigs.

clue.text: Old soldiers after the big fish ?

definitions.text: Old soldiers after the big fish ?

parts.words: Old soldiers after the big fish
parts.note: men who fished for the large predatory pike, and also soldiers of old armed with long spears

explanation.surface: Veterans going fishing for a large catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry of old armed with long spears called pikes; the fish shares the weapon's name.

clue.text: A town of some atmosphere in the North

definitions.text: A town of some atmosphere in the North

parts.words: A town of some atmosphere in the North
parts.note: a seaside resort of northern Scotland, with a word for atmosphere at its centre

explanation.surface: A northern town with plenty of character.
explanation.walkthrough: Nairn is a resort on the Moray Firth, Scotland; AIR sits between the two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: A small town and resort on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: With enough and to spare, man sleeps uneasily

indicators.note: a sleeper tossing uneasily is restless, so the letters toss into a new order

explanation.surface: A man with more than he needs still sleeps badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampleness is abundance, a plentiful supply with extra left over.

clue.text: Do you get the point, chief ?

parts.note: taken as written
ye is the old form of you
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A question asking a boss whether he follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point, here N for north; 'get' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the senior or most respected member of a group.

clue.text: A note from Mr. Verdant on return

parts.note: verdant means green, so this invented gentleman is Mr Green
on returning one is back

explanation.surface: A letter received back from a man named Verdant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a banknote, not a letter: the American dollar bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an American dollar bill, from the green ink on its reverse.

clue.text: Mean-or simply lacking some cash ?

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the named letter is dropped from the word simply

parts.note: s is the old abbreviation for a shilling, a sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone short of money asks whether that is all it means.
explanation.walkthrough: S stood for a shilling in pre-decimal British money; 'lacking' removes it from SIMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to suggest or signify it without saying it outright.

clue.text: That envious render in ancient Rome

definitions.text: That envious render in ancient Rome

parts.words: That envious render in ancient Rome
parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Antony shows the rent in Caesar's cloak made by the envious conspirator

explanation.surface: A jealous man tearing things in old Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony says 'See what a rent the envious Casca made': a render is one who rends or tears.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman conspirator who struck Caesar first, called envious in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Third international's alternative spell

parts.note: the Communist Third International was known by a short name spelt with a C or, alternatively, with a K

explanation.surface: A rival incantation from a third sporting international.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like magic but means spelling: the Comintern was also written with a K.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant spelling of Comintern, the Communist Third International founded in Moscow in 1919.

clue.text: Result of an inverted invitation to play by moonlight ?

indicators.note: inverted means the two words of the invitation swap their order

parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'Boys and girls come out to play, the moon doth shine as bright as day'
the same rhyme's call supplies its first word

explanation.surface: Consequences of a children's rhyme being turned on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out' from the nursery rhyme, with its two words swapped round by 'inverted'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end product of events.

clue.text: Scene of divorce in a ditch perhaps ? How lyrically sad !

indicators.note: in places the divorce city inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests one possible arrangement, so the word ditch is reshuffled

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces

explanation.surface: A broken marriage ending in a ditch is lamented in song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges DITCH to THDIC, and 'in' puts RENO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a song of mourning, so threnodic means mournful in a poetic way.

clue.text: "Do the work that's" (Kingsley)

parts.note: Charles Kingsley's line 'Do the work that's ..., though it's dull at whiles'; the missing word completes it

explanation.surface: A quotation from Charles Kingsley with its last word left blank.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near, meaning closest to hand, completing the Victorian writer's line of verse.

clue.text: Ancestor finds a bit of heaven

definitions.meaning: a forebear in the line of descent
in astrology, the degree of the zodiac rising at the eastern horizon

explanation.surface: Someone's forebear discovers a little paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascendant is a forebear, and in astrology it is the part of the sky rising at one's birth.

clue.text: Sailorboy in a waterproof

definitions.meaning: old slang for a seaman, from their tarred canvas clothing
a heavy sheet of waterproofed canvas

explanation.surface: A young sailor dressed in oilskins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor was once called this, as was tarred canvas used as a waterproof covering.

clue.text: Flocks of teal in the rising waters

definitions.meaning: the collective noun for a group of teal ducks
places where water wells up out of the ground

explanation.surface: Teal ducks flock on a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring of teal is the old venery term for these ducks, and springs are sources where water emerges.

clue.text: Where porpoises find their levels?

parts.note: porpoises swim in groups bearing the same name as institutions where pupils are graded into levels

explanation.surface: A question about how porpoises are sorted by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of porpoises or fish, and also places of education with classes at different levels.

clue.text: Zola's role in the Dreyfus case

definitions.text: Zola's role in the Dreyfus case

parts.words: Zola's role in the Dreyfus case
parts.note: Emile Zola's open letter J'accuse charged the army with framing Dreyfus

explanation.surface: A history question about a French novelist and a famous scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola's letter J'accuse made him the one bringing charges against the authorities.

clue.text: Marks for speech

definitions.meaning: signs placed over letters, such as acute and grave
distinctive ways of pronouncing, regional voices

explanation.surface: Scores awarded for a speaking performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Diacritics are marks over letters, and regional pronunciation patterns are how people speak.

clue.text: Lisa right fashionable and royal

parts.note: Lisa calls up Mona, as in Leonardo's Mona Lisa
chic means stylish or fashionable

explanation.surface: A woman named Lisa is described as stylish and regal.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or relating to a monarch, so kingly or queenly.

clue.text: A beast makes some trouble out of the ring

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters are stirred into another order

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: An animal causes a bit of trouble outside the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' is a verb on SOME plus O, the ring; 'out of' means made from.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest deer, a big North American animal.

clue.text: Follow that mouse, before it strikes one!

definitions.text: Follow that mouse, before it strikes one!

parts.words: Follow that mouse, before it strikes one
parts.note: in Hickory Dickory Dock the mouse climbs the clock before the clock strikes one

explanation.surface: Chase that mouse before the clock chimes one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' refers to the clock, not the mouse; a run-up is the approach before a strike or event.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach or period leading to an event, as the mouse's climb preceded the chime.

clue.text: A' cosy home-loving girl ?

parts.note: a nest is a snug home, as in a love nest

explanation.surface: A girl who loves staying in her snug home.
explanation.walkthrough: Nesta is a girl's name; 'loving' just links the home to the A beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh girl's name, a form of Agnes.

clue.text: It's an odd blemish

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a blemish is peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a discoloured mark or spot that spoils a surface.

clue.text: In those days a glimpse of stocking was shocking

definitions.text: In those days a glimpse of stocking was shocking

parts.words: In those days a glimpse of stocking was shocking
parts.note: Cole Porter's Anything Goes begins 'In ... days a glimpse of stocking was looked on as something shocking'

explanation.surface: A remark on prim times past, when showing a stocking scandalised.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for long ago, the adjective Cole Porter's song uses for those prudish times.

clue.text: Bootless

parts.note: bootless is an old word for useless, from boot meaning profit or advantage

explanation.definitionFit: Bootless means without profit, achieving nothing, so useless.

clue.text: Mysterious spies cast as getaway people

indicators.note: mysterious suggests something obscured, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Secret agents in disguise are cast as people on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: People who escape, whether from bonds or from reality, are escape artists.

clue.text: This saw has a number added

parts.note: ten is a number
on means attached or added, as in tacked on

explanation.surface: A carpenter's saw with a figure stamped on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This saw' defines by naming the tenon saw, a fine carpentry saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small saw with a stiffened back, used for cutting joints.
